The genes showing the strongest cross-region correlation with ALS disease duration were mainly immune/myeloid genes whose expression was higher in shorter-duration (faster-progressing) cases. The strongest single gene was HAVCR2/TIM-3 (cross-region Stouffer z=-8.83, p=1.09e-18, FDR=1.89e-14; negative slopes in cervical, lumbar, and thoracic cord). Other top negative-duration genes were CHIT1 (z=-8.27, FDR=1.14e-12), APOC2 (z=-8.16, FDR=1.86e-12), CD37 (z=-8.00, FDR=5.36e-12), PLA2G7 (z=-7.94, FDR=6.81e-12), followed by SLC29A1, HLA-DMB, CCRL2, NCF2, NCKAP1L, CDCP1, LILRA2, OLR1, ARL11, and SYK.

The strongest positive-duration genes, higher in longer-duration (slower-progressing) cases, were IL17D (z=6.48, p=9.05e-11, FDR=1.48e-8), IGSF1, B3GAT2, PAH, TRIL, DAAM2, SERPINB9P1, LDLR, GSTM5, and PHGDH.

Interpretation: HAVCR2 and CHIT1 are the clearest biomarker candidates from this analysis. The dominant negative-duration signature is consistent with microglial/macrophage activation, antigen presentation, oxidative-burst, and lipid/lysosomal inflammatory biology in rapidly progressive ALS. These are postmortem transcriptomic associations, not yet validated prospective predictive biomarkers.
